name: Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition Disease / Pseudogout
definition: Crystal arthritis caused by calcium pyrophosphate deposition, producing acute attacks, chronic inflammatory arthritis or incidental chondrocalcinosis.

typical: Acute hot swollen joint, commonly knee or wrist
Can mimic gout or septic arthritis

redFlags.item: Septic arthritis must be excluded in a hot swollen joint

investigations.principle: Synovial-fluid analysis can identify CPP crystals and exclude infection.
investigations.MRI: Ultrasound may show crystal deposition; MRI is not routine.

green: Address associated metabolic disorders where relevant
amber: NSAID, colchicine or corticosteroid strategies require individualized risk review.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Sandhi-shotha/Vata-Rakta-like phenotype may be documented only after infection is excluded.

patientEducation.summary: Crystal arthritis caused by calcium pyrophosphate deposition, producing acute attacks, chronic inflammatory arthritis or incidental chondrocalcinosis.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
